purpose: Cidofovir is used to treat a serious eye infection called cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis, which mainly affects people with weakened immune systems, such as those with HIV/AIDS. It helps stop the virus from damaging your eyesight and potentially causing blindness. It is a powerful antiviral medicine used when other treatments may not be enough.
how_it_works: The virus that causes CMV retinitis needs to copy itself to spread and cause damage. Cidofovir works by blocking a key tool the virus uses to make copies of itself, called DNA polymerase. By blocking this tool, the medication stops the virus from multiplying and spreading further in your body.
common_side_effects: The most common and serious side effect is kidney damage, so your kidney function will be closely monitored. You may also experience nausea, vomiting, fever, hair loss, decreased white blood cell counts, and eye problems such as reduced eye pressure or vision changes. Some people notice a decrease in appetite or feel generally unwell.
warnings: This medication can cause serious kidney damage, so it must always be given with another medicine called probenecid and with plenty of IV fluids to help protect your kidneys. You should NOT take cidofovir if you are also using other kidney-damaging drugs like certain antibiotics or NSAIDs. It can also lower your white blood cell count, increasing infection risk. This medicine may cause birth defects, so reliable contraception is essential during and after treatment. Men should use contraception for several months after treatment ends.
typical_dosing: Cidofovir is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion directly into a vein, usually by a healthcare professional in a clinic or hospital. The typical starting dose is 5 mg per kilogram of body weight once a week for two weeks, followed by a maintenance dose of 5 mg/kg every two weeks. Each infusion is given alongside probenecid tablets and IV fluids to protect your kidneys.
